title: A Echo for the Machine
premise: Kestrel Galloway, the fourth clone of a murdered signal officer, has spent twelve years alone maintaining Beacon Station 7, a relay nobody claims. When a distress transmission arrives in Vessic—a language exterminated along with its speakers two centuries ago—Kestrel realizes the beacon was built by the original Galloway to one day carry a peace message hidden in that dead tongue. Hunted by a warship that wants the message destroyed and haunted by fragmented inherited memories of the original's murder, Kestrel must decode and deliver it. In the end, Kestrel broadcasts the message, exposing the war's engineered origins, and chooses to stop being a copy by becoming the first of something new: a family formed with the Vessic-descended refugees who answer the signal.
about_author: Dominic Galloway is the pen name of a former radio technician who spent six years maintaining remote communications arrays in the North Atlantic before turning to fiction. They write about lonely signals, inherited grief, and the families people build out of static.

chapters.title: The Quiet Frequency
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. A day in the rhythm of solitude: calibrating the beacon, talking to the station AI, tending the original's grave-marker garden. Establishes the clone's routine invisibility and quiet dread of being decommissioned like obsolete equipment. Emotional beat: loneliness mistaken for safety.

chapters.title: A Language With No Speakers
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. The distress signal arrives—structured, urgent, unmistakably Vessic. Kestrel cross-references archives and finds the original Galloway studied Vessic before the murder. First intrusion of inherited memory fragments: a corridor, a knife, someone saying 'don't send it.' Emotional beat: wonder curdling into fear.

chapters.title: Inheritance of Static
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV, interleaved with memory-flashbacks from the original. Decoding begins using the original's hidden notes sewn into the station's maintenance logs. Kestrel learns the beacon was never a relay—it was a vault. Emotional beat: the unsettling intimacy of living inside a dead person's plan.

chapters.title: The Ship That Answers No One
chapters.summary: POV shifts to Commander Ilsa Rehn of the warship Meridian, ordered to silence any transmission from Sector 7. She suspects her own command is lying about why. Her crew includes a young Vessic-descended linguist, Tam, who doesn't know his own heritage. Emotional beat: duty beginning to crack.

chapters.title: Don't Send It
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. The decoded message reveals the war was manufactured—the original Galloway found proof and was killed for it. A memory fragment surfaces whole: the original hiding the message inside the beacon's foundation code. Emotional beat: grief for a self Kestrel never was.

chapters.title: Two Ships Passing
chapters.summary: Alternating POV, Kestrel and Rehn. The Meridian arrives in orbit; Kestrel must stall while finishing decryption. Tam secretly hails the station in broken Vessic, and Kestrel answers—the first conversation in that language in two hundred years. Emotional beat: connection across impossible distance.

chapters.title: What the Original Knew
chapters.summary: Rehn's POV. Ordered to destroy the station, she instead boards it under pretext of inspection and confronts Kestrel. Together they find evidence her own admiralty ordered the original's murder. Tam defects to the station. Emotional beat: choosing conscience over chain of command.

chapters.title: Countdown on a Dead Tongue
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. The Meridian's loyalist faction seizes the ship; bombardment imminent. Kestrel races to translate the final cipher block as memories flood faster than they can process them—nearly losing their own identity inside the original's. Emotional beat: identity at stake, self dissolving.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Climax, all three POVs converging. Under fire, Kestrel transmits the full message fleet-wide in Vessic and Standard simultaneously. Tam's voice joins the broadcast, translating live. The truth of the manufactured war spreads through every receiver in the system. The Meridian's crew mutinies rather than fire. Emotional beat: a single voice becoming many.

chapters.title: First of Something New
chapters.summary: Resolution, Kestrel's POV. Weeks later: refugee ships arrive carrying Vessic descendants answering the signal. Rehn faces inquiry but finds allies; Tam begins teaching the language again. Kestrel plants a new garden—not a grave-marker but a doorstep—and lets the clones' cycle end with them. Emotional beat: belonging, finally chosen rather than assigned.
